title: Course Units
text: This is the complete course topics we will cover:

title: Course Units
text:
Unit 1: Programming with R
Learn programming basics with R: data types, data structures, variables, programming structures, etc. Find here the slides.

title: Course Units
text:
Unit 2: Exploratory Data Analysis
Learn data visualization, transformation and exploration with the help of the tidyverse ecosystem using ggplot2 and dplyr to explore and transform your data, the unit is divided in three chapters…

Part 1. Visualization
Part 2. Transformation
Part 3. Exporatory Data Analysis

title: Course Units
text:
Unit 3: Data Wrangling
Wrangle your data using tidyverse’s tidyr package, work with relational data using dplyr and wrangle special data types with the help of forcats, lubridate or stringr. Also learn how to import different sources of data into your enviornment with the help of libraries such as readr or readxl.

Part 1. Importing Data
Part 2. Organizing Data
Part 3. Wrangling Data Types

title: Course Units
text:
Unit 4: Modelling
Basic introduction to data modelling with the use of linear models such as linear regression. Find here the slides.

title: Course Units
text:
Unit 5: Communication
Learn how to develop reproducible reports and automate your documentation tasks to improve share of results. Find here the slides.

Packages covered in the course

From the tidyverse world…

Rmarkdown and Quarto for reporting
infer for testing statistical inference and boostrapping

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
Task: complete a data analysis project from start to finish using Claude Code, an AI assistant that runs in the terminal. For better understanding it is suggested to do it in groups of 2 students.
Operating system: every step that differs between systems is shown in two tabs, macOS and Windows. Click the tab for your system. Your browser remembers the choice for the whole page.

text:
Plan and time budget








Step
Content
Time




0

10 min

Your role: supervisor



Claude writes and runs the code, but you are responsible for the analysis. Read the plans, the scripts and the outputs, and question anything that looks wrong. Only the work you can explain will be considered yours.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
section: 0.1 Check that R, RStudio and Quarto are installed
text:
0.1 Check that R, RStudio and Quarto are installed
Open RStudio and run this in the console:
R.version.string
quarto::quarto_version()   # only works if the 'quarto' R package is installed
You can also check Quarto from the terminal with quarto --version. Recent versions of RStudio already include Quarto. If it is missing, install it from quarto.org/docs/get-started.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
0.2 Open a terminal

macOSWindows


Open Terminal (Spotlight → type “Terminal”). You can also use the Terminal tab inside RStudio.


Open PowerShell (Start menu → type “PowerShell”). You can also use the Terminal tab inside RStudio, but check that it is PowerShell and not CMD.
Native Windows also needs Git for Windows. Check it with:
git --version
If the command is not found, install it from git-scm.com/downloads/win and open a new PowerShell window afterwards.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
0.3 Install Claude Code

macOSWindows


Recommended (native installer):
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Alternatives, if the installer does not work:
# Homebrew
brew install --cask claude-code

# npm (requires Node.js 18 or later)
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code


Recommended (native installer, in PowerShell):
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
Alternatives, if the installer does not work:
# WinGet
winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode

# npm (requires Node.js 18 or later)
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
If you prefer a Linux-like environment you can also use WSL and follow the macOS instructions inside it. This is optional, and the native installer is enough for this activity.



Close and reopen the terminal, then check the installation:
claude --version






Troubleshooting: “claude: command not found”






macOSWindows


The installer places the program in ~/.local/bin. Add it to your PATH and reload the shell:
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc


Close all PowerShell windows and open a new one so the updated PATH is loaded. If it still fails, add %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin to your user Path variable (Start → “Edit environment variables for your account”). You can also run claude doctor once the command is found to diagnose the installation.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code

text:
0.4 Create the project folder and start Claude
Each pair creates the folder proyecto-airbnb/, opens the terminal inside it and runs claude.

macOSWindows


mkdir ~/proyecto-airbnb
cd ~/proyecto-airbnb
mkdir data
claude


mkdir $HOME\proyecto-airbnb
cd $HOME\proyecto-airbnb
mkdir data
claude



The first time, your browser opens so you can log in with your CUNEF account. When you come back to the terminal, Claude Code is waiting for your first message.






Useful commands inside Claude Code










Command
What it does




/help
Shows the available commands


/init
Generates the CLAUDE.md project memory file


/clear
Clears the conversation context (start a fresh task)


/agents
Lists, creates and edits agents


/exit or Ctrl+C twice
Leaves Claude Code


Shift+Tab
Cycles through the permission modes

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
0.5 Get the data
Go to insideairbnb.com/get-the-data, find Madrid and download the files from the most recent snapshot: listings.csv.gz, reviews.csv.gz and calendar.csv.gz. Move them to the data/ folder of your project:

macOSWindows


mv ~/Downloads/*.csv.gz ~/proyecto-airbnb/data/
ls data/


Move-Item "$HOME\Downloads\*.csv.gz" "$HOME\proyecto-airbnb\data\"
dir data



Do not unzip them: readr reads .csv.gz files directly.






Alternatively, ask Claude to download the data for you (see the prompt in Step 1). If its network access is blocked, download the files manually as shown above. The URLs on the site change with every snapshot, so always take them from the web page.



Checkpoint 0

claude --version prints a version number
You are logged in with your CUNEF account
data/ contains the three .csv.gz files

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
1.1 Project memory with /init
Inside Claude, run:
/init
Claude explores the folder and creates CLAUDE.md, a “memory” file that it reads at the start of every session. Open it in an editor and add the course style rules, for example:
## Course conventions
- Language: R with the tidyverse. Use readr to read files and janitor::clean_names().
- Plots: ggplot2 with theme_minimal().
- Code comments in Spanish.
- Scripts live in scripts/, data in data/, figures in figuras/, reports in the project root.
- Never modify the raw files in data/.






Everything you put in CLAUDE.md applies to every later request, so you do not have to repeat the style in each prompt.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
1.2 First assignment: import and clean
Give Claude this prompt (adapt it if you wish):

Download the Madrid data from Inside Airbnb (or use the files already in data/), import them with readr, apply clean_names(), convert price to a number, parse the dates with lubridate and join listings with reviews. Write it as a script in scripts/01_import_clean.R, run it and fix any errors.

Claude writes the script, runs it and fixes failures. You review what it did. Check these typical pitfalls:

price comes as text such as "$1,250.00". It should end up as a numeric column (readr::parse_number()).
The reviews table has many rows per listing (one per review). Joining it directly with listings multiplies rows. A sound approach is to summarise the reviews per listing first (number of reviews, date of the last review) and then join by listing_id = id.
Missing values, prices equal to 0 and extreme prices (outliers).
Which column holds the neighbourhood? In recent snapshots neighbourhood can be empty or inconsistent, while neighbourhood_cleansed is usually the reliable one.







Ask Claude to explain



If you do not understand a line, ask: “Explain what this block does and why you chose it.” Using Claude to learn is part of the exercise.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
1.3 Permission modes
Claude Code asks for your supervision at different levels. Switch between them with Shift+Tab:







Mode
What Claude does




Default
Asks permission before each action (editing a file, running a command).


Plan mode
Only reads and proposes a plan; it does not touch anything.


Accept edits
Applies file changes without asking, but still asks before anything else, such as running commands.


Auto mode
Works autonomously.









On some Windows terminals Shift+Tab may not cycle modes. In that case try Alt+M, or start Claude with claude --permission-mode plan. Start in default mode. Use auto mode only when you are happy to review the result afterwards, and never on folders that contain anything you cannot afford to lose.



Exercise (2 min). Switch to plan mode and ask: “Plan how you would check the quality of the cleaned data.” Read the plan and then switch back to default mode.
Checkpoint 1

CLAUDE.md exists and contains your course style rules
scripts/01_import_clean.R runs without errors
There is a clean, joined dataset (for example saved as data/listings_clean.rds)
You have tried the different permission modes

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
2.1 Ask Claude to create eda-report

Create a skill called eda-report for exploratory data analysis of a cleaned dataset. Instructions it should include: use readr to read files; produce summaries of the variables, missing values and distributions; make plots with ggplot2 and theme_minimal; save the PNG files in figuras/; and finish the analysis with a summary of the 3 main findings.

Then open .claude/skills/eda-report/SKILL.md and read it. It should look similar to this:
---
name: eda-report
description: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) of a cleaned tabular dataset in R. Use when asked for an EDA, a data overview or an exploratory report.
---

# EDA report

1. Use `readr` to read the data files (never base R `read.csv`).
2. Summarise structure and quality: dimensions, variable types, missing values, duplicates.
3. Describe the key variables: distributions of numeric variables and counts of categorical ones.
4. Explore relationships with the target variable (for example, price against room type, neighbourhood and capacity).
5. Make all plots with `ggplot2` and `theme_minimal()`. Save every plot as a PNG in `figuras/`.
6. End with a summary of the **3 main findings**, each backed by a figure or a number.






Project vs. personal skills. A skill in .claude/skills/ of your project is available only in that project. To reuse it in any project, place it in your personal skills folder:

macOSWindows


~/.claude/skills/eda-report/SKILL.md


%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\eda-report\SKILL.md






If Claude does not recognise /eda-report right away, restart the session (/exit, then claude again).
Checkpoint 2

.claude/skills/eda-report/SKILL.md exists and you have read and understood it
Typing /eda-report appears in the list of commands

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
3.1 The built-in Explore agent
Ask Claude to use it:

Use the Explore agent to go through the project and summarise what it contains: files, scripts, data and the current state of the analysis.

Observe that the main conversation only receives the summary, not every file the agent read.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
3.2 Create your own reviewer agent
Run /agents, choose to create a new project agent, or simply ask Claude:

Create an agent called reviewer in .claude/agents/reviewer.md. Its role is a critical reviewer of data analyses. It must audit the model assumptions, the treatment of the data and the code. It should only read files, never modify them.

The result is a file like this:
---
name: reviewer
description: Critical reviewer of data analyses. Use it to audit model assumptions, data handling and code, and to get a second opinion that challenges the analysis.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
---

You are a sceptical senior data scientist reviewing a colleague's work. You never modify files.

Review three areas:

1. **Data treatment**: units and types, missing values, outliers, joins that duplicate rows, filters that remove data.
2. **Model assumptions**: linearity, normality and constant variance of residuals, influential points, multicollinearity, choice of the response variable (price vs. log price).
3. **Code**: correctness, reproducibility (paths, seeds), style and clarity.

Return a prioritised list of problems (critical / important / minor), with the file and line, and one concrete suggestion for each. Do not praise; question.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
3.3 Use it
Reference the agent by name in your prompt:

Use the reviewer agent to audit scripts/01_import_clean.R and the cleaned dataset.

Decide which of its remarks are valid and fix them. You will use the agent again in Step 4 to validate the model.
Checkpoint 3

You used the Explore agent and read its summary
.claude/agents/reviewer.md exists
The reviewer audited your cleaning, and you applied at least one improvement

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
4.1 Exploration
Run the skill on the clean data:
/eda-report
You should get an exploratory analysis with plots saved in figuras/ and the 3 main findings.

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
4.2 Model and answer
Fit and interpret a model that answers the question:
price ~ room_type + neighbourhood + accommodates
using lm() and the broom package (tidy(), glance(), augment()). Suggested prompt:

Fit price ~ room_type + neighbourhood + accommodates with lm() in scripts/02_model.R. Use broom to get the coefficients and the fit statistics. Interpret the main coefficients in plain language: how much more or less does each factor cost, holding the others fixed? Check the residual diagnostics.

Then validate with your agent:

Use the reviewer agent to review the model: assumptions, treatment of outliers and whether using log(price) would be better. Report the problems and fix the important ones.







Things worth discussing




With neighbourhood the reference level is arbitrary, and with many levels the table is long. How do you present it clearly (for instance, the 10 most expensive and cheapest neighbourhoods)?
Is the residual distribution reasonable? What changes if the response is log(price), and how does the interpretation of the coefficients change?
What does the R² tell you? Which important variables are not in this model?

title: Final Project: Data Analysis with Claude Code
text:
4.3 Communication: a reproducible report
Put everything together in a Quarto document with the data, the plots from /eda-report, the model and the conclusion. Suggested prompt:

Create informe.qmd (Quarto) that answers “What determines the price of an Airbnb listing in Madrid?”. Include: a short description of the data and the cleaning, the figures from figuras/, the model with a table of coefficients and its interpretation, and a clear conclusion. It must run from scratch. Then render it to HTML.

Render it from the terminal (or let Claude do it):
quarto render informe.qmd --to html






PDF output instead of HTML





PDF needs a LaTeX distribution. The simplest way is TinyTeX, which Quarto installs for you:
quarto install tinytex
quarto render informe.qmd --to pdf
If you have problems, HTML is perfectly valid.



Open the result:

macOSWindows


open informe.html


start informe.html



Your report must answer the question clearly: state in a few sentences what drives the price and by how much.
Checkpoint 4

/eda-report produced plots in figuras/ and the 3 findings
The model is fitted, interpreted and validated by the reviewer agent
informe.qmd renders without errors to HTML (or PDF)
The conclusion answers the research question
